reviews.reasoning: Numbering re-derived, not inherited: web_mt_offset_map.json gives Ps 103 rule identity, web_verses 22 / mt_verses 22, mt_title_verses empty, note identity_confirmed_by_kjv_note_on_v1, so the WEB title pseudo-ref web:Ps.103.0 = oshb:Ps.103.1 pairing in the refs array is arithmetically correct and, per the owner ruling, the sanctioned opening-row form; citation_sweep.py returns 0 problems on this row. The title splice לְדָוִ֨ד (oshb:Ps.103.1) collates at the byte tier and is verse-initial in MT 103:1, ahead of the summons clause, so the row's description of it as a prefix inside MT v.1 rather than a counted title verse is byte-true. The self-summons splice בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.103.1) also collates at byte tier. The seam at 5|6 is tier-1 and independently re-derived: oshb:Ps.103.3-oshb:Ps.103.5 run a chain of definite participles with 2fs suffixes addressed to the summoned soul, and oshb:Ps.103.6 opens with the third-person predicate עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת with יְהוָ֑ה as its named subject; addressee and grammatical person both change at that seam. The rejected_alternative is one sentence and is factually right: the barchi-nafshi clause is inside MT 103:1 itself, not confined to the title. check_web_quotes.py is GREEN over this row's WEB quotes and check_refs_mirror.py finds no unmirrored out-of-span verse. Observations, not defects: (a) check_universals.py flags the substrate signal's phrase 'with no separate title verse number' as a digit-free absence claim, but the proposition is a per-psalm numbering fact carried by the authority file (mt_title_verses: []), not a swept universal, so I read the flag as a heuristic false positive; (b) the clause the row calls the inclusio's opening half recurs byte-identically at oshb:Ps.103.2 inside this same span (skeleton sweep of the 4-word clause: 5 verses in Psalms - MT 103:1, 103:2, 103:22, 104:1, 104:35), which strengthens rather than weakens the row. No selah, no ketiv/qere and no pe/samekh layer is claimed or available here; pmarks_Ps.json lists paseq segs at MT 103:1, 103:17 and 103:22, which are seg-layer only and do not touch the quoted verse bytes.

The span's substance holds. עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת (oshb:Ps.103.6) collates at the byte tier and is verse-initial; the participial predicate with יְהוָ֑ה as subject is the correct reading of the bytes and agrees with the WEB rendering “Yahweh executes righteous acts, and justice for all who are oppressed.” (web:Ps.103.6), so the second-person-to-third-person shift the row uses as its opening driver is real. The close at 10 is likewise supported: oshb:Ps.103.9 and oshb:Ps.103.10 each carry a doubled negation pair (2 verses, 2 negative particles each), so calling them a negated-accusation pair is byte-warranted, and oshb:Ps.103.11 opens a new construction. Confidence medium is calibrated. citation_sweep.py, check_marks.py, check_refs_mirror.py and check_web_quotes.py return 0 flags between them on this row (4 checkers) and the dual-cite question does not arise (Ps 103 is an identity psalm). The defect is register, not evidence. One further precision note that does not rise to a challenge: the substrate signal says the summons clause opens the preceding unit, but in MT numbering oshb:Ps.103.1 opens with לְדָוִ֨ד and the clause is second - the statement is true only in WEB numbering, where the title is the separate pseudo-verse web:Ps.103.0.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] closes with a positional row reference, which the standing register purge bans outright in row prose.
challenges.evidence: The field ends with the words 'opening the row before it' - a positional row reference of exactly the banned form ('the row before this one'), used where the campaign register requires a verse-anchored formulation. The anchor it needs is already present in the same clause (oshb:Ps.103.1), so the cure is a deletion of the trailing 4 words, not a re-argument. Nothing in the evidence base changes: בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.103.1) collates byte and עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת (oshb:Ps.103.6) collates byte, and the contrast between them survives the edit intact.

reviews.reasoning: Both Hebrew splices in this row collate at the byte tier (כִּ֤י כִגְבֹ֣הַּ שָׁ֭מַיִם at oshb:Ps.103.11; כִּי עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ at oshb:Ps.103.14), the span tiles cleanly, and the 11|14 internal reading is sound: oshb:Ps.103.11, oshb:Ps.103.12 and oshb:Ps.103.13 form a 3-verse comparative tricolon (kaf-prefixed comparanda in all 3, correlative apodoses), and oshb:Ps.103.14 keeps Yahweh as the grammatical subject of יָדַ֣ע, so holding 14 with the simile chain rather than with the transience movement is defensible and the rejected_alternative states that correctly. The span itself I do not contest. What fails is the row's stated differentiator for the 10|11 seam and its two particle-function labels; both are refutable from the bytes and from the WEB renderings the row itself quotes. Note for repair: the 10|11 seam is shared with the row ending at web:Ps.103.10, so a warrant replacement is one edit installed on both sides of the seam, and the replacement has to survive the same v10 counterexample that kills the original.

challenges.claim: The seam warrant asserts that the preceding declarative catalog does not use a comparison construction, but the seam-adjacent verse oshb:Ps.103.10 uses the same inseparable-kaf comparison twice.
challenges.evidence: The rationale's differentiator is the phrase 'a comparison construction the declarative catalog of web:Ps.103.6-web:Ps.103.10 does not use'. Byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, MT 103:10 reads כַ֭חֲטָאֵינוּ and כַ֝עֲוֺנֹתֵ֗ינוּ (oshb:Ps.103.10, both byte tier) - the kaf of norm/comparison prefixed to 2 nouns in 1 verse, i.e. 2 tokens over 1 of the 5 verses in oshb:Ps.103.6-oshb:Ps.103.10, and it is the LAST verse before the seam. The WEB rendering the row itself quotes makes the same point in English: “He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities.” (web:Ps.103.10). The comparative force in the row's own exhibit at oshb:Ps.103.11 sits in the same morpheme class - כִגְבֹ֣הַּ (oshb:Ps.103.11, byte tier) is kaf prefixed to the same kind of comparand - so the feature named as absent on one side of the seam is present on the other side, in the immediately adjacent verse. The seam may well survive on other tier-1 grounds (the 3-verse correlative simile tricolon at oshb:Ps.103.11-oshb:Ps.103.13), but the warrant as written does not.

challenges.claim: Both particle-function labels in observed_substrate_signals[0] are wrong: ki is not the comparison particle at 103:11, and the ki spliced from 103:14 is the second of 2 in that verse and is complementizing, not causal, on the row's own WEB rendering.
challenges.evidence: (a) The field calls כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.103.11, byte tier) 'the comparison particle'. The comparison at MT 103:11 is carried by the inseparable kaf of כִגְבֹ֣הַּ (oshb:Ps.103.11, byte tier), not by כִּ֤י; the WEB the row quotes distinguishes them explicitly - “For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his loving kindness toward those who fear him.” (web:Ps.103.11) renders כִּ֤י as For and the kaf as as. (b) MT 103:14 contains 2 tokens of that particle (verse-initial and post-זָ֝כ֗וּר; oshb:Ps.103.14, byte tier). The row splices the SECOND one, in כִּי עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ, and labels it 'a plain causal use'. On the row's own WEB quote, “For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.” (web:Ps.103.14), the causal sense belongs to the verse-initial token (For) while the token actually spliced is rendered that - a complement clause governed by זָ֝כ֗וּר. The signal therefore mislabels the function of the very token it quotes, and does not disambiguate which of the 2 tokens is meant.

challenges.claim: device_notes carries a positional row reference banned by the standing register purge.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads 'hinges toward the grass-and-flower transience imagery of the next row without changing grammatical subject'. 'the next row' is a positional row reference; the register rule requires verse-anchored cross-row wording, and the correct anchors are already used in this row's own rationale (web:Ps.103.15-web:Ps.103.16). The substantive claim is unaffected and byte-true: the subject of יָדַ֣ע at oshb:Ps.103.14 is Yahweh, and אֱ֭נוֹשׁ (oshb:Ps.103.15, byte tier) is the new subject.

reviews.reasoning: Span and seams hold. The 14|15 seam is a genuine grammatical-subject change (אֱ֭נוֹשׁ opens oshb:Ps.103.15 against Yahweh as subject of יָדַ֣ע at oshb:Ps.103.14), and the 18|19 seam is tier-1 (oshb:Ps.103.19 opens יְֽהוָ֗ה בַּ֭שָּׁמַיִם הֵכִ֣ין, byte tier, an enthronement declaration). Both Hebrew splices collate at the byte tier: וְחֶ֤סֶד יְהוָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.103.17) and וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Ps.102.13). The cross-psalm arithmetic is correct and I re-derived it: Ps 102 is a shift+1 psalm, so web:Ps.102.12 = oshb:Ps.102.13 as the refs array has it, and citation_sweep.py raises only the WARN-tracked in-field dual pairing note, which the toolkit scope ruling explicitly excludes from challenge. The comparative force claim (plain conjunctive vav at 103:17 vs vav-plus-independent-pronoun at 102:13) is correct on the bytes and appropriately hedged. Two smaller defects stand, both in the row's own grammatical bookkeeping and its register; neither disturbs the span.

challenges.claim: The rationale says the vav-clause pivots back to Yahweh as subject, but Yahweh is not the grammatical subject anywhere in MT 103:17.
challenges.evidence: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, MT 103:17 opens וְחֶ֤סֶד יְהוָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.103.17, byte tier): a construct chain in which יְהוָ֨ה is the nomen rectum, so the subject is the chain itself, and the second colon's subject is the suffixed וְ֝צִדְקָת֗וֹ (oshb:Ps.103.17, byte tier). Yahweh is the possessor in both of the 2 cola and the subject of neither. The row uses 'subject' as a technical term elsewhere in the same field ('pivots back to Yahweh as subject' set against the change to man at web:Ps.103.15), and the contrast verse it names does have Yahweh as subject - וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה ... תֵּשֵׁ֑ב (web:Ps.102.12 = oshb:Ps.102.13, byte tier) - which sharpens rather than excuses the slip. WEB agrees with the bytes: “But Yahweh’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children,” (web:Ps.103.17) makes the loving kindness, not Yahweh, the subject.

challenges.claim: device_notes closes with the words 'elsewhere in this part', an unanchored file/part reference of the class the register purge bans.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads '... the adversative turn at web:Ps.102.12 elsewhere in this part'. The verse anchor web:Ps.102.12 is correct and sufficient by itself; the trailing 'in this part' names the authoring part rather than a text unit (the two psalms it spans, 102 and 103, are exactly one writer part), and on the only other available reading it would name a book division the strategy calls a book, not a part. Either way the phrase is unanchored bookkeeping register in row prose, curable by deleting 3 words with no evidentiary loss.

reviews.reasoning: The span, the unit_type and the high confidence are all right. All 4 Hebrew splices collate at the byte tier: יְֽהוָ֗ה בַּ֭שָּׁמַיִם הֵכִ֣ין (oshb:Ps.103.19), בָּרֲכ֥וּ יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.103.20), בָּרֲכִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ps.103.22) and בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.103.1). The number contrast the row draws is byte-true: oshb:Ps.103.20 and oshb:Ps.103.21 open with the plural imperative and oshb:Ps.103.22 carries the plural imperative first and the singular בָּרֲכִ֥י last, so the widening-then-returning summons is a real feature and not an imposed shape. The tier call is also correct as far as it goes - I recomputed the two clauses and they are unequal at byte, unequal at NFD, unequal at accent_stripped (meteg U+05BD is retained by that tier) and equal at skeleton, exactly as the row says. What is wrong is the row's characterisation of HOW they differ, stated twice (rationale and observed_substrate_signals[1]). Two observations that are not defects: the same clause recurs byte-identically at oshb:Ps.103.2 and the skeleton occurs in 5 verses of Psalms (MT 103:1, 103:2, 103:22, 104:1, 104:35), so the row's 'across the 2 verses' is a scoped comparison of 2 named refs rather than a book count and I do not read it as a count-object violation; and the single-quoted mention of the imperative in the rationale is a mention, not a WEB quotation, so it does not owe curly quotes.

challenges.claim: The row states twice that the opening and closing clauses differ only in the trailing accent mark on the final word; byte comparison shows 3 of the 4 words differ, across 4 accent codepoints, one of which is an addition with no counterpart.
challenges.evidence: Both clauses spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collated at byte tier against their own verses: בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.103.1) and בָּרֲכִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ps.103.22). Word-by-word codepoint diff: word 1 differs (U+05A3 ACCENT MUNAH at 103:1 vs U+05A5 ACCENT MERKHA at 103:22); word 2 differs (U+05AD ACCENT DEHI at 103:1 vs U+059D ACCENT GERESH MUQDAM; U+0597 ACCENT REVIA at 103:22 - note that is a substitution PLUS an added accent with no counterpart in 103:1); word 3 is identical; word 4 differs (U+0591 ACCENT ETNAHTA at 103:1 vs U+05BD POINT METEG at 103:22). That is 3 differing words of 4 and 4 accent-codepoint differences, not 1. The row's phrase 'only in the trailing accent mark on the final word' is therefore false as written, and the supporting gloss 'an expected verse-final cantillation difference' describes only the word-4 difference; the word-1 and word-2 differences are ordinary mid-clause accentuation changes, not verse-final effects. The row's conclusions survive - the differences are all accent-layer, so the 'not a textual variant' reading and the skeleton-tier claim are both correct - but the substrate description has to be recut in both fields in one edit.
